nodes.title: Register and sign in
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Hashed passwords, cookie sessions, ~/.local/share/openchq or OPENCHQ_WEB_DATA.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Online lobby
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Signed-in sockets see who is online.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Bot room
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Play a bot opens one room. The player sits on the chosen side. The other seat is Bot.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Human room
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Invite, decline, and accept. Accept opens one room with two human seats.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Shared clock flag
nodes.work: Already in web/server. Hold and Run are visible to every seat in the room. Pieces do not move yet.
nodes.prove: Covered by the harness node.

nodes.title: Lock the scaffold with WEB_OK
nodes.work: Add web/test/run.mjs. It starts the server on 127.0.0.1 with a temporary OPENCHQ_WEB_DATA and a free port. It must not use port 8787. It registers two users, rejects a short password, rejects a wrong password, rejects a duplicate name, opens a bot room, runs and holds the clock, leaves, invites, declines, accepts, and sees the room end when the other socket closes. A socket with no cookie gets HTTP 401. The process prints WEB_OK and exits 0. It kills only the server it started.
nodes.prove: node web/test/run.mjs prints WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Terrain and sites on the server
nodes.work: Read the extract the way the desktop archive did: OPENCHQ_DATA, then local/data_root.txt, then data/. Load data/tmap.bin as 320 by 136 nibbles with row stride 162, and data/sites.json. GET /api/board returns width, height, cell ids, and sites. Washington and Moscow are the capitals. The JSON has no image bytes and no path to WORLD_MAP.png, the stills, or the unpacked executable.
nodes.prove: The harness requests /api/board and requires 320 by 136, both capitals, and no forbidden payload. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Paint the cell grid in the page
nodes.work: The match canvas draws cell ids from /api/board. Ocean, shallows, land, city, and capital are distinct colors. The schematic remains only when the extract is missing, and the page says the extract is missing. Do not draw the original picture.
nodes.prove: A pure painter test checks the color of ocean, shallows, city, and capital. The harness still prints WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Rooms outlive the process
nodes.work: A room is a row, not a Map entry. web/server/rooms.mjs owns a rooms table on the same SQLite database; the lobby writes on create and on every clock change, deletes only on a real end, and restores every stored room paused at boot. Idle rooms older than 24 hours are pruned. A restart never resumes a clock.
nodes.prove: The harness starts a bot room, runs the clock, kills the server, restarts it on the same data directory and reconnects: the same room id comes back, held, with the caller still in its seat. Removing the store write makes that assertion fail.
nodes.evidence: Committed with the storage pass; WEB_OK with the restart block in web/test/run.mjs.

nodes.title: Timing and prices live in one file
nodes.work: config/game.json holds every player-facing number: round length, pay cadence, starting pool, prices, fuel reserve and burn, sight radius, enemy route steps, HITS. web/server/rules.mjs loads it once per process and exposes roundSeconds(), payEvery(), priceOf(), landPace(), seaAccepts(), sightCells(), enemyRouteSteps(), startPool(). No module may hard-code a round length, a price, a sight radius or a terrain cost.
nodes.prove: The harness imports rules.mjs and asserts the loaded values match config/game.json, that landPace refuses wasteland and charges slow ground, and that the server reports the configured round length. Changing config/game.json changes the reported value without touching code.
nodes.evidence: Round length set to 5 s by the owner on 2026-11-06: at 1 cell per round the Washington-Moscow march is ~104 cells, about 8.7 minutes, where 0.14 s made a 24-second war.

nodes.title: Opening pieces
nodes.work: A match module in JavaScript places Blue at Washington and Red at Moscow, plus one ship each, for 1918, 1942, 1986, and the concealed era. 2023 places no pieces. Creating a bot or human room attaches this match. The room view includes the caller's pieces.
nodes.prove: The harness opens a 1986 bot room and sees four pieces, then a 2023 bot room and sees none. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Server tick
nodes.work: The server advances a running room one round at a time. Tests call the tick function directly and do not sleep. A held clock does not move pieces. One running round is the same 0.14 second live interval, and tests do not wait that interval.
nodes.prove: The harness holds a room for five direct ticks and sees no movement, then runs it for one tick. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Land orders
nodes.work: A seat orders its own land piece to a cell. The piece walks one cell per running round. X wraps. Y does not. Wasteland is refused. Ocean and lake are transport. Forest, mountain, polar, jungle, and shallows take longer than open ground. The pace ratio stays unnamed.
nodes.prove: The harness orders the Blue army one open step and sees that cell after one running tick. A wasteland order is refused. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Sea lanes
nodes.work: Ships move on the lane graph. The server may read the unpacked executable on the machine that hosts the server and cache waypoints it computed. The browser never receives that file. A land piece ordered from sea to sea follows the lanes. A land-to-land order stays on land.
nodes.prove: The harness sails the Blue ship one lane step and checks the land-to-land order did not become a sea route. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Bot seat
nodes.work: In a bot room the empty seat marches its army toward the player's capital and sails its ship once when the path is empty. It does not repath the ship every round.
nodes.prove: The harness runs a bot room and sees the bot army take a path toward the player capital and the bot ship take one path. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Two human seats
nodes.work: In a human room neither seat is given bot orders. Each socket may order only its own side. A forged side is refused.
nodes.prove: The harness accepts an invite, orders each side, and proves a forged side does not move the other army. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Stop short and fight
nodes.work: Two pieces never stop on the same cell. They stop one cell short. A shot happens every other round of one continuous fight. No damage number is stored or shown. Removal waits until a later measured hit count. Do not invent that count in this node.
nodes.prove: The harness places two hostile armies on adjacent cells, ticks, and sees them still on those cells with a shot note that has no digit. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Per-seat view
nodes.work: A seat sees its own pieces, enemy pieces within Chebyshev 8 with X wrapping, and only the first three steps of an enemy route. A still submarine is omitted. In the concealed era the other side is omitted until its capital is found. Hidden pieces are absent from the JSON.
nodes.prove: The harness puts an enemy army 9 cells away and asserts it is missing from the view, then moves it to 8 cells and asserts it is present. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Buying
nodes.work: Land and aircraft buy on a friendly city. Ships buy on a friendly dock. Before the clock has ever run, the purchase does not spend the pool. After the match is running, it spends the stand-in price and marks that city unready with no duration. Infantry is 1 billion. A tank is 2. Ships, submarines, and aircraft are 2. A nuke is refused. Two pieces cannot share a cell.
nodes.prove: The harness buys a tank after the clock has run and sees the pool fall by 2, then sees a nuke refused. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Oil ownership
nodes.work: Wells start with the country they are in. USA is Blue. Russia matches USSR and is Red. Any other named region stays that name. A unit standing on a well captures it. Do not copy production ratings. The well rate stays unknown.
nodes.prove: The harness steps a Blue unit onto a Red well and sees the owner become Blue. The payload does not contain the word production. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Docks and wells must exist as sites
nodes.work: data/sites.json carries only city, capital and facility records. Docks are terrain id 1 (150 painted cells) and wells come from the oil resource list, so a room's site list has no dock for a ship to buy at and no well for a side to hold. Merge docks from the painted terrain and wells from the resource positions onto match.sites at room creation, keeping each record's id, name, x, y and kind, and leave any site whose kind is unknown as it is. Do not invent a production rating for a well.
nodes.prove: The harness opens a 1986 room, counts docks and wells on the match site list, buys a ship at a dock, and captures a well by standing on it. A room created with no extract still opens (empty site list) instead of throwing.

nodes.title: Income into the pool
nodes.work: City income is one billion per city held. Oil income is one billion per well the side holds. On rounds 25, 50, 75, and so on, add both levels to that side's pool. Capitals are not cities. A shortage does not pay. A finished match does not keep paying.
nodes.prove: The harness ticks to round 25 with a known city count and well count and checks the pool. Round 24 does not pay. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Fuel per side
nodes.work: Each side has its own reserve, starting at 10000 and burning 1 on each running round that side has no unit on a well. Zero stops that side only. The other side still moves, buys, and collects income. Standing on any well refills that side's reserve.
nodes.prove: The harness sets Blue's reserve to 1, ticks once, and sees Blue stopped while Red still moves. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: Hold both capitals
nodes.work: The match ends when one side owns both capitals. Further ticks do not move pieces, pay income, or burn fuel. The room tells both seats who won.
nodes.prove: The harness gives one side both capitals, ticks, and sees the winner and a frozen board on the next tick. WEB_OK.

nodes.title: A thousand rooms inside one round
nodes.work: Prove the target scale on this host, with numbers, not adjectives. tools/bench-rooms.mjs measures a full tick pass over N rooms and the cost of snapshotting them to the store. Assert in the harness that 1000 rooms of 8 pieces tick and snapshot well inside the 0.14 s round budget, and that a held room costs nothing: no tick, no write. Report the headroom multiples. Do not shrink the model to make the number look good.
nodes.prove: node tools/bench-rooms.mjs 1000 8 reports headroom above 10x for both the tick pass and the snapshot, and the harness prints WEB_OK including that assertion.

nodes.title: Reconnect
nodes.work: A dropped socket does not delete the room or free the seat: the match is held, kept in the store, and reserved for that account, and it does not tick, pay or burn fuel while nobody watches. That pause-and-keep half already ships (done ahead of this node, proved by the harness: drop a seat, the room survives paused, the connected seat can run it again). What remains here: a returning socket gets the same filtered view of its seat it had before (own pieces, sight 8, first three enemy steps), and the absent seat's standing orders are still in the match and still execute when the clock runs.
nodes.prove: The harness closes one socket, connects again as the same user, and sees the same room id and its own pieces. WEB_OK.
nodes.note: pause-on-empty shipped with the room_store pass

nodes.title: Remove the Godot tree from this branch
nodes.work: Delete the Godot project files from the web branch only after every dependency is done and WEB_OK still passes. Do not delete the desktop-godot branch. Do not touch github main.
nodes.prove: The harness still prints WEB_OK. project.godot is gone on this branch. origin/desktop-godot still exists.

nodes.title: Send what changed, not the whole view
nodes.work: A full seat view every round measured at 2.6 MB per round for 2000 seats (~18 MB/s), which is the real cost of 1000 concurrent games. Send per-round deltas: changed pieces, new and cleared route steps, and a periodic full resync. Keep the payload honest - hidden pieces stay absent. Record before and after bytes per round in the harness.
nodes.prove: tools/bench-rooms.mjs and the harness report bytes per round for a 1000-room tick before and after, and the delta payload is at least 5x smaller while a client that missed a delta still gets a correct view after the resync.
nodes.evidence: lobby keeps a shadow of the last frame per seat and sends {op:'delta'} with only changed pieces, gone ids, changed routes and site ownership; a whole frame on connect, every 20 rounds, on a clock change, after a gap, or when half the board moved. The page merges deltas and asks {op:'sync'} when a round does not follow. Measured with local/delta-cost.mjs: 27,048 B/round whole frame vs 4,744 B/round delta = 5.7x. web/test/nodes/view_deltas.mjs merges the deltas a real socket received and asserts the merged board equals the server's own full frame.

nodes.title: More than oil, and still no invented rates
nodes.work: The successor will differ from the 1990 game here on purpose. Add resource kinds as data (config/game.json) with a generic holding + consumption model instead of one-off oil code, keep per-side reserves, and gate each kind by era. Any rate the owner has not set stays unnamed and unplaced rather than guessed. This is an owner-designed expansion, not a recovery of the original.
nodes.prove: The harness asserts a second resource kind can be configured, held, consumed and shown without new code paths per kind, and that an unset rate is refused rather than defaulted to a number.
nodes.evidence: config/game.json carries its resource kinds as data: `resources.fuel` and `resources.steel`, each with a reserve, a per-round burn and (where it applies) an era gate. web/server/resources.mjs holds, spends and burns any kind by name - no branch per kind except the legacy seat.fuel/seat.dry mirror - and `produce()` returns an error when a kind has no `rate`, never a default. economy.upkeep no longer knows a reserve, a burn or a field name: it captures wells and hands the round to upkeepResources. The seat view and the player's purse carry every kind the scenario has, with a null rate where none was recovered. web/test/nodes/resources.mjs proves a second kind held/spent/dry/gated/shown, proves a THIRD kind (`tin`) configured at runtime works with no new code, and proves the unset rate is refused (with a rate set in a temp config the payout happens, so the assertion can fail).

nodes.title: Make the match length a decision, not a leftover
nodes.work: Measure a real match end to end: rounds to first contact, rounds to a capital, rounds between income payments, and wall-clock minutes at the configured round length. Report the curve. If it is too short or too long, change config/game.json and re-measure; do not tune individual numbers by feel and do not change the rules to make a clock look right.
nodes.prove: A recorded run reports wall-clock minutes for a 1986 bot match and the income cadence in seconds, and the harness asserts the match takes at least the owner's chosen floor (config) before a capital falls.
nodes.evidence: docs/PACING.md: two bot-vs-bot runs at 5 s/round. First contact round 85 (7.1 min) with the shipped bot, 33 captures, 24 kills, no winner inside 1200 rounds. Round length is a wall-clock knob; the front is the real problem.

nodes.title: Decide single instance or many, with numbers
nodes.work: One process holds 2000 sockets and ticks 1000 rooms inside the round budget. Decide whether the product needs more than one instance (uptime, region, load). If yes, the room store moves to Postgres and rooms are sharded per instance with a sticky socket; if no, record that the volume-pinned single instance is the accepted design and what would overturn it.
nodes.prove: A written decision in docs/SCALE.md with the measured numbers it rests on, and the harness still prints WEB_OK on whichever path was chosen.
nodes.evidence: docs/SCALE.md with measured numbers: 1,000 rooms cost 9.79 ms per round (0.2% of a core at 5 s), 114 KB heap per 40-piece room (111 MB at 1,000), 4.0 MB/s egress with deltas vs 23.0 MB/s without. Decision recorded: one instance until a measured trigger, because the first ceiling is egress and the single SQLite writer is what forbids a second instance today. The multi-instance path names its migration surface (saveRoom/loadRooms/pruneRooms), the lease, and edge routing by room id, and marks which parts already exist.

nodes.title: A deploy must not drop a live game
nodes.work: Every deploy restarts the process and closes every socket. Rooms survive (they are rows), but a player mid-match is disconnected by a build. Add a drain: the server answers a local-only POST /api/drain by holding every running room and replying when no seat is connected, and tools/fire.sh calls it before railway up with a timeout. If the drain does not clear in time, deploy anyway and say so. Never make the page poll to find out - the socket close is the signal.
nodes.prove: The harness starts a room with a connected seat, calls drain, sees the clock hold and the response deferred, closes the seat, sees drain return, and confirms the store has the room held. A drain with no rooms returns at once.
nodes.evidence: main.mjs catches SIGTERM/SIGINT: stops the ticker, beginDrain marks every running room with a human seat to resume, broadcast tells the seats 'op:bye', flushAll writes every room, then exit. rooms.saveRoom persists that flag and loadRooms restores a marked room running with its saved clock. The page reconnects by itself with backoff and says 'Reconnected. The match is where you left it.' Proven live: SIGTERM logged 'drained 1 rooms, 1 will resume, 1 seats told', and across the restart the board went round 14 -> 16 with clock running and no button pressed.

nodes.title: A player can actually give an order
nodes.work: The server accepts op "order" but nothing sends one: the page has no click-to-command. Select a piece on the canvas, hover shows the route and its cost in rounds, click commits and sends {op:"order",piece,to:{x,y}}. The reply is acknowledged in place; a refusal is shown as the message the server returned, never swallowed. Own pieces only, own seat only.
nodes.prove: Harness: a socket order moves the piece on the next tick and a refused order returns a reason that reaches the page. Browser: click a piece, click a destination, the route preview appears and the piece moves after a round.

nodes.title: Buying exists, so 2023 is playable
nodes.work: economy.buy is implemented and unreachable: there is no "buy" op and no panel. Add the op with the same seat checks as "order", and a panel listing the era's units with prices read from config/game.json, disabled when the seat cannot pay or has no friendly city/dock for that kind. 2023 opens with no army, so without this the empty era cannot be played at all. A nuke stays refused and says so.
nodes.prove: Harness: in a 2023 room, buy an infantry at a friendly city - cash falls by the configured price and the piece appears; a nuke is refused with a reason; a second purchase in an occupied cell is refused. Browser: the panel shows prices and the piece appears on the board.
nodes.evidence: lobby 'buy' op with the same seat checks as 'order'; shopFor(era) serves prices from config. Two real bugs found on the way: ownership was seeded lazily inside economy.buy so a 2023 board had no friendly city at all, and purchases were free until the clock first ran (fill the board, then press Run). Now seeded at open and always charged. Harness covers price, occupied-cell refusal and the nuke refusal; browser verified: 'Bought an infantry at 39,35. Pool 39.' with 1 piece on the board.

nodes.title: The screen must show what the rules are doing
nodes.work: The room view carries no cash, fuel or income state, and the canvas draws a 320x136 map at 2x so a piece is about four pixels. Add cash, per-side fuel, rounds until the next payment and owned city/well counts to the view; show them in a HUD. Camera zoom, follow and panning are shipped under the `camera` node; this node is the cash, fuel and countdown HUD only.
nodes.prove: Harness: the room view reports cash and fuel that change when the economy does. Browser: with the extract present, a piece is visibly a piece at 4x, the HUD shows cash and the countdown, and panning across x=0 does not tear.
nodes.evidence: The room panel draws pool, fuel and 'payment in N rounds' from seat {cash, fuel, payIn, payEvery}; the shop row shows every era unit at its config price, disabled when unaffordable, with the nuke's refusal written on the button. Browser-verified in a 2023 match.

nodes.title: Every rule the server applies must be visible
nodes.work: Shots resolve silently, captures are invisible and a finished match shows nothing but a note. Send the tick's events to the seats (shot, capture, blocked, over) and render them: a shot flash on the fighting cells, a capture toast naming the site, a blocked-order marker, and an end screen naming the winner with the round. Nothing invented: a shot still has no damage number, so the cue shows that a shot happened, not how hard.
nodes.prove: Harness: a tick over a fighting pair and a capture emits events that reach the seat socket. Browser: the flash, the toast and the end screen are visible, and the shot cue contains no digit.
nodes.evidence: web/server/log.mjs turns a round's events into lines per seat and filters them with the seat view, so a concealed-era enemy cannot leak through the log; lobby sends {op:'log'} each round and keeps the lines on the room so a reload restores them (welcome carries room.log). Page paints 'round N - ...' with contact lines de-duplicated. Verified live: 'round 1 - took Washington', 'round 8 - an enemy is in sight at 86,50', 'round 25 - paid 18 from 13 cities', and the same lines after a reload.

nodes.title: Fog of war has to look like fog
nodes.work: The server filters the view but the page draws an evenly lit map, so the fog is invisible and the sight rule teaches nothing. Draw seen terrain lit, remembered-but-unseen terrain dimmed, and never-seen terrain darker still; outline the sight radius of the selected piece. Hidden enemy pieces stay absent - do not draw a placeholder where one might be.
nodes.prove: Harness: pure helper maps a visibility class per cell for a given sight set. Browser: moving a piece reveals a ring and the map is visibly darker outside it; no enemy marker appears outside the radius.
nodes.evidence: render.sightTable/rememberSeen/paintFog: lit, remembered and unknown ground at two darkness levels, Chebyshev with the X wrap, radius from the board payload. Tests in web/test/nodes/render.mjs.

nodes.title: Land units cross water in transports
nodes.work: Today a land piece walks across ocean at the slow pace, which is a stand-in for a mechanic the original had: land units form transports, and transports are vulnerable. Give a land piece ordered across water a transport state (a sea piece carrying it), moving on the lane graph, killable while it carries cargo, and landing the cargo on a coast cell. Keep every duration in rounds against the configured round length.
nodes.prove: Harness: a land unit ordered across the Atlantic receives a transport, is not removed when it is not attacked, lands on the far coast, and a transport that is engaged loses its cargo. A land unit ordered to land never enters transport.
nodes.evidence: move.syncTransport derives cargo from the cell (water = ocean/docks/shallows); embark/landed events; combat.resolve lets a transport fire nothing and sinks it on the first exchange. Soak 1000: 767 embarked, 603 landed, match still resolves (blue r466).

nodes.title: Aircraft are a resource, not a piece
nodes.work: 1942 and later: a mission makes the aircraft inactive for a number of rounds, combat air patrol scrambles near an enemy mission, a strike returns no damage number but must resolve something, carriers extend the reach. Express every duration in rounds against the configured round length and keep the archive's rule that a carrier aircraft cannot paradrop. Where the original gave no number, the stand-in stays in config and is labelled.
nodes.prove: Harness: a mission sets an inactive-until round and the aircraft does not move before it; a patrol near an enemy mission goes inactive; an aircraft with no carrier reach cannot strike. Numbers come from config.
nodes.evidence: web/server/air.mjs: strike costs 8 rounds, scramble 4 (booklet counts, config under air), an inactive aircraft cannot be ordered or move, a mission needs a friendly city/dock/ship within reach (reach 10 is labelled a stand-in), and a strike sinks caught cargo but invents no damage. Test: web/test/nodes/air.mjs.

nodes.title: The 1986 kit, minus the numbers nobody has
nodes.work: Nukes, recon and killer satellites, intel scans, foreign aid and cease-fires. Keep the archive's restraints: capitals have an exclusion radius, crews refuse to target home ground, launches stop after three, the first user is penalised, and nuclear winter can lose for both sides. Where the original never printed a radius, cost or damage, the value lives in config as an explicit stand-in or the action stays refused.
nodes.prove: Harness: a nuke is refused by default config; with the flag set it paints wasteland and applies the penalty; intel reveals and tells the opponent; the three-launch limit stops the fourth. No invented number appears in code.
nodes.evidence: web/server/late.mjs: era-gated tool list (1918/1942 hide the 1986 kit, concealed start shows oil only), intel reveals and tells, satellite reveals quietly, aid flips a city, cease-fire accepted and changes nothing, nuke refused by default with the booklet's three-launch limit and a home-ground guard. Test: web/test/nodes/late_kit.mjs.

nodes.title: Accounts a stranger can own
nodes.work: Sign-up accepts an email-shaped handle, but there is no way to change a password, no session expiry, no rate limit on login or register, and no way to close an account. Add password change and sign-out-all, expire idle sessions, rate-limit failures per handle and per address, and delete an account's rooms and sessions when it closes. Keep the cookie flags as they are.
nodes.prove: Harness: a wrong password repeated hits the limit; an expired session is refused; a changed password invalidates old sessions; closing an account removes its rooms. Rate-limit state survives a restart or says plainly that it does not.
nodes.evidence: auth.mjs limits a caller to 5 failures per 15 min keyed on address+name, then locks 5 min and answers 429 'Too many attempts. Try again in N s.'; sessions carry expires_at (30 days), userForToken deletes a stale row, pruneSessions sweeps at boot and hourly; POST /api/password verifies the current password, refuses short or unchanged ones, rehashes, and ends every other session. Page has a Change password form. web/test/nodes/account_ops.mjs covers all of it; browser verified 'Password changed.'

nodes.title: A battle has to have a result
nodes.work: A 1000-round soak with both seats played fired 2270 shots and left 400 pieces alive: combat.resolve only counts shots, and nothing in the server ever removes a piece, so armies are immortal and no match can end. Give the exchange an outcome. Where the archive prints no damage, the outcome is a rule the user sets in config - e.g. a piece that has been under fire for N consecutive rounds is destroyed, or odds per exchange - never a number invented in code. Read the value from config/game.json, keep it in rounds, and say in player-facing text that it is a stand-in.
nodes.prove: Harness: two adjacent pieces firing for the configured number of rounds destroy exactly one of them, the survivor keeps its cell, the store reflects the removal, and a piece that breaks contact resets the clock. Soak: a 1000-round both-sides match produces destroyed units and a winner.
nodes.evidence: combat.resolve removes the defender after HITS (6, config/game.json) shots in one continuous fight - the archive's own rule from docs/POLISH_LOOP.md. Soak 1000: 82 units destroyed, match ends round 466 with a winner.

nodes.title: Cities change hands, and that is income
nodes.work: economy.capture only ever considers an oil well - a piece standing on a city or a capital changes nothing, so all 62 cities are decorative and income cannot grow or shrink. Make occupation the capture rule for city, capital and dock: a piece alone on a site owned by the other side (or neutral) takes it, the site keeps one owner at a time, a capital is held while a piece stands on it and lost when it leaves, and income reads the result. Keep wells as they are.
nodes.prove: Harness: a piece walks onto a neutral city and owns it; an enemy piece takes it back; a capital held for a round is lost when the piece steps off; the pay round uses the new count. Soak: sites change hands and income curves move with the map.
nodes.evidence: economy.occupy (called by tick between resolve and upkeep) transfers city/dock/capital ownership to the side standing on it; capitals are never seeded. Soak 1000: 8 captures including Moscow and Washington changing hands twice.

nodes.title: Digging in and repairing, as words not numbers
nodes.work: Entrenchment is infantry only, its bonus was never recovered, and a move order clears it (docs/POLISH_LOOP.md). Repair is a state that holds while a piece stands on a friendly city or dock. Every piece carries one of the five words the unit list uses: moving, digging, repairing, inactive, idle.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/combat_depth.mjs pins the refusals, the state words, that an order clears digging, and that the seat view carries state, entrenched and transport.
nodes.evidence: move.pieceState/entrench/repair; view.viewPiece carries state; occupy rewritten to one path over pieces after the capacity bench fell to 9.6x (now 11.2x at 1000 rooms).

nodes.title: A board you can read
nodes.work: 320x136 at 2x makes a piece four pixels. Whole-cell zoom from 2x to 8x about the cursor, pan by right-drag and arrow keys, follow the selected piece, and an X pan that runs past the edge because the painter tiles the seam.
nodes.prove: render clampZoom/centerOn/panBy/zoomAt plus app.js wheel, pointer and key handlers; the seam stays continuous because paintCells wraps column lookups.
nodes.evidence: render.mjs camera helpers + app.js wiring; render test pins the zoom floor/ceiling, that a zoom keeps the cell under the cursor, and that centring is exact.

nodes.title: A mass of force has to be decisive
nodes.work: Overrun shipped as a count comparison. Measured: it does not break an even front. The open half of this node is concentration - see bot_concentration.
nodes.prove: Two pieces against one removes the defender faster than one against one; a massed attack breaks a line in the soak; a match played by the bot on both sides ends inside 600 rounds with a winner.
nodes.evidence: Overrun implemented as a comparison, not a threshold (strictly more friendly pieces on the defender's cell than the defender has, both combatants excluded), config-gated, tested in web/test/nodes/combat.mjs. A/B at 1200 rounds: 24 destroyed without it, 27 with it, captures unchanged at 33, no winner either way - the rule fires at a bulge and cannot fire along an even line.

nodes.title: The bot has to mass, not march
nodes.work: Measured: with the shipped bot on both sides a 1200-round match produces one even line, 27 kills and no winner. Overrun cannot fire on an even line. The bot sends every piece at the enemy capital, so it never has surplus anywhere. Teach it to pick one point of the enemy line, gather the pieces that can reach it, and push there - concentration is a behaviour, not a rule, so it costs no fidelity.
nodes.prove: A bot-vs-bot match ends inside 600 rounds with a winner, and the timeline shows a breakthrough (a round where one side loses 3+ pieces and the other loses none).
nodes.evidence: bot.focusTarget: the army masses on the weakest enemy cell. A bot-vs-bot match now ends - red at round 441 (36.8 min at 5 s), first contact round 41, 44 destroyed, 42 captures - against no winner in 1200 rounds before. Reproducible across three runs. bot test rewritten to check the path closes on the chosen target, not the capital.

nodes.title: The original's bottom bar
nodes.work: WORLD.PIC is 320x200: the map is 320x136 starting at y=6, rows 0-5 are black, and the chrome is a black band from y=142 with a bevelled box 87x50 at (1,142) that says TIME LEFT over a bar. Rebuild that band in HTML/CSS at the original's proportions (87/320 of the map width, 50/320 of it tall), drive the bar from the round clock, and put the payment countdown in it. Measured geometry, not remembered.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/chrome.mjs asserts the box is 87/320 of the map width and 50/320 tall at every scale, that the label is TIME LEFT, and that the bar goes from full to empty as a round runs down and that the payment countdown matches rounds until the next payday.

nodes.title: The original's lettering
nodes.work: FONTS.CHQ is in COMMAND/ and has never been decoded. Decode it into a glyph atlas (or prove what it is and say so), serve it only where the extract exists, and use it for the chrome label and the round log at whole-pixel sizes.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/fonts.mjs asserts the decoded atlas has the glyph count the file implies and that a known string renders to distinct non-empty bitmaps; the page falls back to a system font when the extract is absent.

nodes.title: Units that look like the original's
nodes.work: BLOCKED until a disassembler is usable in-session: UNITS.PIC's top rows are editor art on a ~12 px pitch, and the on-map marker glyphs are not obviously there - the table that maps a unit to its marker is in the draw routine inside CHQ_unpacked.EXE. With REA's Ghidra provider working (GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR is now in the profile config), read that routine, cut the markers, and draw them per domain and side. (Now depends on chq_disassembly: the marker table has to be read out of the EXE first. What is already known: UNITS.PIC is 320x200 in 16 EGA colours, its top 24 rows are two 10-tile bands of 12x12 sprites - the same figures repeated on white, blue and cyan plates, i.e. palette variants of UI sprites - and the rest is window chrome and large art. ANIMS/*.PAN decode to large battle sprites, not 1-cell markers. So the markers are not in the art files.)
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/unit_icons.mjs asserts each domain (infantry, armour, sea, submarine, aircraft) and each side resolves to a distinct marker bitmap cut from the sheet, with the shapes fallback when the extract is absent.

nodes.title: A disassembler that actually runs
nodes.work: unit_icons is blocked on one fact that only CHQ_unpacked.EXE holds: which marker the game draws for each unit type and side. The REA MCP provider is not present in-session, but Ghidra 12.1.4 is installed at ~/tools/ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC and binutils objdump handles 16-bit DOS. Get a usable 16-bit disassembly of CHQ_unpacked.EXE (Ghidra analyzeHeadless with the x86:LE:16 real-mode language, or objdump -b binary -m i8086), locate the code that draws a unit marker on the world map, and write the table it reads (unit type -> marker bitmap, per side) to Command HQ/modern/extracted/data/unit_markers.json. If the table cannot be found, record what the routine does instead and say so.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/disasm.mjs asserts a real artifact exists: either unit_markers.json with one entry per unit type and side plus the address the table was read from, or a written finding naming the routine and the instruction that draws the marker. The test fails if the artifact is a guess: it checks every marker entry decodes to a bitmap of the game's map scale (1-5 px per side) and that both sides differ.

nodes.title: Names on the board
nodes.work: The original kept place names in its panels; this page puts them on the map once the camera is close enough to read them. Add LABEL_ZOOM (4 px/cell), visibleLabels(sites, view) returning only cities on screen with a label box clamped inside the viewport, and paintLabels(ctx, atlas, labels) drawing from the decoded FONTS.CHQ atlas at whole-pixel scales with a one-pixel shadow. No atlas, no labels.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/labels.mjs asserts nothing is labelled at the whole-earth fit, that labels appear at zoom with one per city and none for unnamed sites, that every label box stays inside the viewport, that a city off screen is dropped, and that without an atlas paintLabels draws zero pixels.

nodes.title: Whose ground is it
nodes.work: The original shipped two views of the same earth: terrain (WORLD.PIC) and political (OMAP.PIC). CBR-REGN.DT0..DT4 hold the region controller per era and CBR-SET.DAT the 84 sites; read what they actually encode before drawing anything. Add a terrain/political toggle to the page that colours a city's ground by who holds it and says what the colours mean; if the region geometry cannot be read, say so in the code and keep the toggle to cities only rather than inventing borders.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/political.mjs asserts the two views differ, that every political colour is one of the measured ones, that a site with no controller stays neutral, and that the toggle returns to the terrain palette unchanged.

nodes.title: Crossing with an escort
nodes.work: A transport that meets a warship sinks; the player has no way to screen one. Add an order that puts a warship on the same route as a transport (an escort), so the transport stops being alone, and have the seat view and the round log say when a transport is crossing unscreened. No new numbers: the sink rule and the movement rules already exist.
nodes.prove: web/test/nodes/escort.mjs asserts an escorted transport is not reported as unscreened, an unescorted one is, that the escort order is refused for a non-warship or a non-transport target, and that the log names the escort when it forms.
